source.context: National parks in India are International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) category II protected areas. India's first national park was established in 1936, now known as Jim Corbett National Park, in Uttarakhand. In 1970, India had only five national parks. In 1972, India enacted the Wildlife Protection Act and Project Tiger in 1973 to safeguard the habitats of conservation reliant species. Further legislation strengthening protection for wildlife was introduced in the 1980s.
source.title: List of national parks of India - Wikipedia

source.context: Ganweriwala was the 5th largest city[9] within the Indus Valley Civilisation and is believed to have been a major centre from 2600 to 1900 BC.[9][12] The Indus Valley Civilisation was a Bronze Age Civilisation[13][14] which at its zenith had an estimated population of 5 million.[13] Together with Mesopotamia and Ancient Egypt, it was one of the earliest complex civilisations,[13][14] and of the three, was the most extensive.[13][14] Ganweriwala was one of the largest cities within the Indus Valley Civilisation but is the least explored.[8][9] Ganweriwala is believed to have followed the typical Indus Civilisation town planning.[15][9] It had an Upper town and a Lower town as is seen in the presence of the two different mounds.[8][9]
source.title: Ganweriwal - Wikipedia

source.context: Biogas is a renewable energy source produced when organic matter breaks down without oxygen, a process called anaerobic digestion. Britannica +1CompositionMethane (CH₄): 50% to 80% (the main energy-rich component)Carbon Dioxide (CO₂): 15% to 50%Trace Gases: Hydrogen sulfide, nitrogen, hydrogen, water vapor, and siloxanes Wikipedia +2How It Is ProducedFeedstock: Organic materials like animal manure, food scraps, crop waste, and sewage sludge are placed in an airtight tank or digestor.Decomposition Stages: Microorganisms break the material down through four stages: hydrolysis, acidogenesis, acetogenesis, and methanogenesis.Capture & Upgrading: The resulting gas is collected. It can be burned raw or purified into biomethane (renewable natural gas) by removing CO₂ and hydrogen sulfide. U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) (.gov) +7Common ApplicationsElectricity and Heat: Burned in engines or combined heat and power (CHP) systems to generate power.Cooking and Lighting: Used directly in household or community biogas stoves.Vehicle Fuel: Compressed into compressed biogas (CBG) or biomethane for transport.Gas Grid Injection: Upgraded and piped into natural gas distribution networks.Organic Fertilizer: The leftover solid and liquid byproduct (digestate) is nutrient-rich and used in farming. ScienceDirect.com +5Learn more about global frameworks and policies via the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Biogas Programme or explore overviews on Wikipedia. If you'd like, let me know what you want to do with biogas:Are you looking to build a small-scale farm or home digester?Do you need details on feedstock requirements or purification methods?
